taxonomy.note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO genus backbone and Flora of North America. Older literature sometimes misapplied Callirhoe pedata to this species.

evidence: Bell County — Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas explicitly reports C. leiocarpa from Bell County.
Travis County — UT Plant Resources Center's Travis County Malvaceae herbarium index includes two C. leiocarpa specimens.
Williamson County — UT Plant Resources Center provides a detailed field-based treatment of C. leiocarpa.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Hays-area historical specimens and user observations support local encounter value, but the PASS does not depend on them.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with life form and the underside of the flower. Tall poppymallow is an annual (sometimes biennial) with one to several erect/weakly erect stems and NO involucellar bractlets beneath the calyx. In bud the calyx lobes meet valvately to form a pointed tip.
diagnostic_traits: typically erect to weakly erect, often 40–95 cm in Williamson material
basal rosette early, often gone by flowering
leaves alternate, palmately 3–7-lobed, becoming smaller/narrower upward
foliage somewhat velvety with simple and mostly 4-rayed stellate hairs
calyx lobes valvate in bud, forming an apiculate/acuminate point
schizocarps smaller than winecup; 10–14 glabrous dehiscent mericarps with prominent beaks and 3-lobed collars

confusers.separator: Winecup is perennial and low/trailing with 3 involucellar bractlets; C. leiocarpa is annual/tall and has no involucel.
Older records can confuse these taxa. C. leiocarpa is annual with auriculate stipules and dehiscent mericarps; true C. pedata is perennial.
Texas poppy-mallow is a stiffly erect perennial with dense 6–8-rayed stellate hairs and an involucel; C. leiocarpa is annual and lacks the involucel.

diagnostic_roles: flower underside proving absence of involucel

installation_guardrail: Do not install until explicit approval.
